title: When to Forget? Complexity Trade-offs in Machine Unlearning
reviewed_version: PMLR volume 267 published original; retrieved exact supplied PDF URL
summary: Two core derivations fail as stated; theorem-level repairs remain open and experiments were not replicated.

problems.title: Lemma B.2 contradicted by private randomized response
problems.evidence: One-step pure epsilon-private Bernoulli output has TV .462117 while bound is about .00802 at the saved parameters.
problems.assumptions_checked: Quadratic loss L2 mu1 on radius1; disjoint nonatomic distributions; algorithm ignores one permitted gradient; privacy global across initial values.
problems.counterevidence: Not a utility-optimal algorithm, but lemma quantifies over the algorithm class before utility; theorem not separately refuted.
problems.impact: Invalidates key lower-bound lemma and supplied proof of inefficient-regime threshold.
problems.repair_scope: Keep integer composition term and rederive bound or add justified algorithm restrictions.

independent_acceptance_check.source_check: Read physical pp3-5 Assumptions1-2, Algorithm1 measurable update and Definition2, p13 Eq26, p14 LemmaB.2/proof and p15 Theorem2 dependency.
independent_acceptance_check.hypotheses: Uniform distributions on disjoint intervals meet nonatomic/flexible support condition. For L2,mu1, quadratic derivative theta-g has magnitude<=2 on[-1,1]. gamma in[0,1] gives the exact stated g-family and positive optimum (1-rf)gamma-rf versus zero. Algorithm1 explicitly permits random seed and arbitrary measurable update, so ignoring the requested gradient and sampling a sign-conditioned bit is admissible at T1.
independent_acceptance_check.independent_derivation: For either output atom and any two initial models, RR probabilities lie between1/(1+e^epsilon) and e^epsilon/(1+e^epsilon), so all likelihood ratios<=e^epsilon: pure privacy globally in input model. TV between the two sign classes is tanh(epsilon/2). Fresh evaluation gives TV and claimed bound below. LemmaB.2 has no low-risk condition; bad utility cannot exclude this algorithm.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_dependency: The algorithm does not disprove the separate minimax lower-bound theorem. It refutes the stated all-private-algorithms lemma used in Eqs33-35. Eq32 keeps ceilingKprime while Eq29 replaces it by a vanishing fractional step; privacy does not imply that continuity. Exact coupling/binomial sublemmas can remain valid.
independent_acceptance_check.severity_and_repair: Major retained for invalid core derivation. Restoring a ceiling alone changes subsequent thresholds and requires a new proof or justified algorithm restrictions; no repaired theorem is claimed.

problems.title: Local loss regularity cannot control unprojected Gaussian and SGD iterates
problems.evidence: Loss .5theta^2+C(|theta|-1)_+^4 meets all local constants and has unique global optimum0; noised expected risk unbounded with C.
problems.counterevidence: Constrained/projected formulation may be repairable; no claim all phase regimes are false.
problems.impact: Core universal upper-bound derivations unjustified for stated function class.
problems.repair_scope: Specify domain/projection, reprove sensitivity/convergence and exact constants.

independent_acceptance_check.source_check: Read physical p3 local ball regularity/unconstrained minimization, p12 Gaussian rule15 and risk/SGD bounds, pp13/15 constants and p16 LemmasC.1-C.2.
independent_acceptance_check.hypotheses: f_C(theta)=theta^2/2+C(|theta|-1)_+^4 is differentiable, globally1-strongly convex, has unique minimizer0, and on[-1,1] derivative magnitude<=1<=L2 for everyC>0. All distribution optima lie at0. The published positive Gaussian variance is fixed by rf,kappa,L,mu, independent ofC.
independent_acceptance_check.independent_derivation: Gaussian noise has positive probability outside[-1,1], so E f_C(G)=sigma^2/2+C E(|G|-1)_+^4 grows unboundedly withC. Recomputed tail moment using normal-tail moment recurrence M_j=a^(j-1)phi(a)+(j-1)M_(j-2), rather than initial quadrature, confirms risk above printed threshold. This attacks the proposed uniform construction, not existence of an alternate algorithm that needs no noise on this data-independent example.
independent_acceptance_check.additional_minor_calculations: Combining Lipschitz noise contribution with LemmaC.2 gives (sqrt(d)kappa*q+q^2)L^2/mu; Eq17 exchanges q powers. Eq18 also removes denominators and changes to e0=L^2/(8mu) without a valid bound. Eq25 loses factor64 because L^4/mu^2=64e0^2. These are formula defects, with constant-only effects distinguished from order claims.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_dependency: Projection/constrained optimization could restore applicability of local assumptions; unprojected Gaussian and SGD are actually printed. Global strong convexity cannot coexist with global finite Lipschitzness on all R^d, so that is not a drop-in fix. The data-independent example does not independently refute all phase regimes.
independent_acceptance_check.severity_and_repair: Major retained for core universal risk derivations outside their domain. A constrained/projected algorithm requires fresh sensitivity, convergence and constants proofs.

problems.title: Zero-query processing and displayed algorithm differ from definitions/proof
problems.evidence: T0 Algorithm1 is identity theta*; Algorithm2 uses noise, undefined initial theta1 and different step schedule.
problems.counterevidence: Gradient-query cost can naturally permit free processing after explicit reformulation.

independent_acceptance_check.source_check: Read physical p4 Algorithms1-2 and Eq5, p6 zero-query claim, p12 constant-step proof.
independent_acceptance_check.independent_derivation: For T0 Algorithm1 returns theta0=theta*. Two distinct optima yield point masses with an event of probabilities1 and0, violating any delta<1 privacy. Noise initialization is absent from that class at zero loops. Algorithm2 initializes theta0 but first loop accesses theta1 and uses2/[mu(t+1)] plus weights, unlike the constant-step proof22-24.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_dependency: Counting only gradient queries can naturally allow free randomized preprocessing; updating the formal class would remove the zero-loop mismatch. Corrected indexing and a distinct proof may support a real algorithm, but the supplied proof does not certify the literal displayed code.
independent_acceptance_check.severity_and_repair: Minor retained for formal definition/algorithm correspondence; no allegation that zero-cost random processing is inherently invalid.

problems.title: Experiments and exact-unlearning discussion exceed demonstrated theorem scope
problems.evidence: Average realized hitting times differ from expected-risk hitting time; exact delta0 outside delta>=1e-8; finite empirical data nonatomic condition fails.
problems.counterevidence: Experiments can illustrate trends without measuring minimax risk.

independent_acceptance_check.source_check: Read physical p5 expected-risk hitting-time definitions6-9, p6 delta range/exact-unlearning discussion, p9 exact-sensitivity disclosure and p17 training-to-threshold repetitions.
independent_acceptance_check.independent_derivation: Averaging runwise threshold hitting times E inf{t:risk_t<=e} is not generally inf{t:E risk_t<=e}. A finite empirical distribution cannot realize every probabilityp in Assumption2. The printed Theorem2 domain delta>=1e-8 does not include exact delta0.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_dependency: Experiments can still illustrate chosen procedures and trends; acknowledged first-order/retain-only restrictions delimit conclusions. No assertion of incorrect plotted raw outcomes or a false limiting theorem is made.
independent_acceptance_check.severity_and_repair: Needs Evidence retained for minimax/exact-limit interpretations; require appropriate separate proof or estimand-aligned analysis.

limitations: Separate inaccessible OpenReview material, external reference proofs and other paper versions not checked.
